profile_text.body:
Coursera is an online learning company whose site describes offerings of online courses, Professional Certificates, Specializations, and degrees, with content from Google, Meta, Anthropic, DeepLearning.AI, and Stanford, among others. It markets Coursera Plus as an annual subscription giving unlimited access to thousands of courses, Specializations, and Professional Certificates. The site frames its programs as job-aligned, designed with employers and universities, and points to pathways into project management, UX design, data science, cybersecurity, data analytics, business analysis, and product management. Named programs include the Google Project Management Professional Certificate, the Google UX Design Professional Certificate, the IBM Data Science Professional Certificate, the IBM Data Analyst Professional Certificate, the Google Cybersecurity Professional Certificate, the Data Analysis with Python Specialization, and the UI/UX Design Specialization.

On AI, the company positions itself as a place to start with beginner-friendly Python or generative AI courses and to browse artificial intelligence as a subject area. Its site names the Machine Learning Specialization, the Deep Learning Specialization, the AI Essentials Specialization, and the AI Engineer Professional Certificate among its better-known offerings, and lists Anthropic and DeepLearning.AI among the providers of its AI-related content.

The company is a for-profit public company founded in 2012, headquartered in Mountain View, California, and traded under the ticker COUR, with SEC CIK 0001651562. Its recorded litigation exposure is in California, with a count of 270. No individual lawsuits, no MCP servers, and no separately tracked products are listed.
